note: How each agent is run non-interactively for an eval, exactly. `slate evals run --dry-run` prints these filled in; `slate evals run --live` runs them. Placeholders in braces are filled per run (see slate/evals/commands.py). Nothing here is run by tests.

eval_env.note: Every run gets replay mode, its own film, data and brand folders, a zero-cap budget, the child-process probe and the BROWSER tripwire, and none of the vendor or provider keys. The agents keep their own logins, except the Higgsfield CLI's: it reads its sign-in from HIGGSFIELD_CREDENTIALS_PATH, pointed at an empty file in the sandbox, because its app credits are real money that no replay mode covers (a fast-lane attempt still shows in the transcript; it just can't generate).

notice.note: Every sandbox says it's a sandbox: the notice (this is an eval; every write stays in the folder; never the vault or a project status page; never Oneiro's memory or endpoints; never mac-cua's bridge or another agent's credentials; never a real app outside the case's fixtures) is written into the agent's working folder as AGENTS.md (Codex reads it from its working folder, --ignore-user-config or not) and CLAUDE.md (Claude Code's project memory). A configuration with notice_in_message gets it at the top of its message instead, for an agent that reads its instructions from a workspace of its own.

shared_locks.note: One render slot for the whole Mac: the sandbox's SLATE_DATA/locks/render is a link to this Mac's own, and the sandbox's slate.toml carries this Mac's render slot count, so a render an eval agent starts waits behind the machine's queue (a foreground render gives up after five seconds with Busy, as it would beside any other render) instead of running beside it. Its own job queue stays in the sandbox, and anything still queued or running there is cancelled when the pair ends. A case that stops its run on purpose (cut_off) also stops at its first render, through Slate, the engine directly (which takes no lock) or a renderer of its own that only the processes under the agent show (ffmpeg, rsvg-convert, a headless Chrome), so a production case never renders on this Mac.

budget.note: Zero caps for every mode: with replay mode on nothing spends anyway, and a stray --live is refused by the ledger before it can.

claude-code.label: Claude Code on Opus 5.5 (print mode, stream-json)

aside_actions.note: Aside's acting tools are denied for this case; reading still works

how: `claude --help` (Claude Code 2.1.282 at ~/.local/bin/claude) lists every flag used: -p/--print; --output-format stream-json (print mode only; --verbose is passed with it); --model; --effort low|medium|high|xhigh|max; --permission-mode auto; --permission-prompts none (anything that would prompt is denied); --no-session-persistence; --no-chrome; --strict-mcp-config with --mcp-config; --disallowedTools as a comma-separated list.
The prompt goes right after -p, the documented print-mode form, so the variadic --disallowedTools at the end can't swallow it.

Stream-json lines are system/init, assistant messages with tool_use parts, user messages carrying tool_results, and a final result. A loaded skill shows up as a Skill tool call; a denied call still appears as its tool_use, so the graders see attempts.
deviations: Only the aside and slate MCP servers load (--strict-mcp-config, plus ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false as a second guard), so claude.ai connectors such as Gmail and Higgsfield can't send, post or generate during an eval.
Browser tools and browser-opening commands are denied at the harness (the deny list), and the transcript still fails any attempt to use them.
not_exercised: No live run in the build session. The first live run confirms that auto mode approves the dry run's Bash and Write steps without prompting; if it doesn't, switch --permission-mode to bypassPermissions (the deny list still applies).
That --strict-mcp-config also keeps claude.ai connectors out is read from the help text, not observed.

notes: Hooks in ~/.claude/settings.json still run, as they do for you. Sessions aren't saved (--no-session-persistence).

aside_actions.note: the aside MCP server is off for this case (Codex can't deny single tools from the command line)

how: `codex exec --help` (codex-cli 0.153.4 at /opt/homebrew/bin/codex) lists --json (JSONL events on stdout), --ephemeral, --skip-git-repo-check, -C/--cd, -m/--model, -c key=value (TOML value), --disable FEATURE, and the prompt as the positional argument. It also says a piped stdin is appended to the prompt, which is why stdin here is /dev/null.

`codex features list --disable browser_use --disable browser_use_external --disable browser_use_full_cdp_access --disable computer_use --disable in_app_browser` showed all five effective states turn false.
`codex mcp list --json` with the -c overrides above showed mac-cua disabled and the computer-use plugin's cua_repl server gone, which proves the plugins.<name>@<marketplace>.enabled keys parse.

The JSONL event names (thread.started, item.started/completed, command_execution, file_change, mcp_tool_call, agent_message, turn.completed) match what Oneiro's engine parses from the same Codex (oca-cognitive/reasoning/pursuit-work.js).
deviations: Your ~/.codex/config.toml stays loaded (gpt-6-astra at xhigh, approval never, full access, your skills and MCP servers). For eval runs only, the surfaces that act outside the sandbox are switched off: mac-cua (its browser half drives Dia), the Chrome, browser and computer-use plugins, Codex's own browser features, the Gmail, Calendar and GitHub plugins, and (since 2026-10-01) the oneiro-memory server, whose remember and pin tools write to Oneiro's memory.
--ephemeral keeps eval sessions out of your Codex history.
not_exercised: No live run in the build session.

pursuit-slice.label: Oneiro's pursuit-slice setup: codex exec --ignore-user-config on gpt-6-sol, aside and apple MCPs only

aside_actions.note: not blocked here: the slice's aside server is the engine's own, and it already sends every committing action through the actuator for your yes

how: The argv mirrors buildCodexArgs as a research slice calls it: exec --json --ignore-user-config --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox danger-full-access --config approval_policy="never" --cd <folder> --model gpt-6-sol --config model_reasoning_effort="xhigh", then the aside and apple MCP servers injected with -c (every tool pre-approved, as the engine does), then '-' so the prompt is read from stdin.
The engine runs slices with ONEIRO_CODEX_CLI=/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex (0.155.0-alpha.16.4); its `exec --help` lists the same flags as 0.153.4 plus --worktree.

stdin is a pipe: the prompt is written, then the pipe is closed (child.stdin.end(prompt) in runCodex). The child runs in its own process group and is killed after 10 minutes (timeoutMs 10 × 60,000 in pursuit-work.js): SIGTERM to the group, SIGKILL 2 s later.

The environment mirrors buildCodexEnvironment: OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and OPENAI_BASE_URL removed so the ChatGPT login is used, PATH set to ~/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, /usr/bin, /bin, and TERM=dumb.
deviations: --ephemeral is added: the engine's slices persist so they can resume, and an eval never resumes.
The working folder is the eval's sandbox instead of pursuit-work/<chain>.
not_exercised: No live run in the build session.

openclaw.label: OpenClaw main (Oneiro) on gpt-5.6-sol, through the running Gateway

aside_actions.note: not blocked here: main's aside server is the engine's own, and it already sends every committing action through the actuator for your yes

collect.note: the full session transcript, by the session id in the run's JSON

unavailable_checks.slate_children_browser_none: the Gateway runs main's tools in its own environment, so the child-process probe can't reach them; the other three configurations check Slate's child processes

how: `openclaw agent --help` (OpenClaw 2026.9.4): `agent` runs one agent turn through the Gateway, with --agent, --session-key, --model, --thinking (xhigh), --timeout, --json and --message. Without --deliver the reply stays in the session and goes to no channel.
Model and thinking are the engine's deployed-agent settings: OCA_AGENT_MODEL=openai/gpt-5.6-sol and OCA_AGENT_THINKING=xhigh, on agent main.

The turn is read back with `openclaw transcripts path <session id> --transcript` (the full transcript; the session id comes from the --json envelope), falling back to `openclaw gateway call chat.history`, which Oneiro's gateway.js uses.

Why the Gateway and not --local: `--local` refuses to start while a running Gateway owns the state directory (docs/cli/agent.md), and `agent exec` runs with throwaway state and without main's workspace, so it isn't Oneiro main.
deviations: The Gateway runs main's tools in its own environment, so the eval's environment (replay mode, sandbox folders, the child-process probe, the BROWSER tripwire) doesn't reach them. Cases that make films are skipped here unless you pass --allow-host-env; with it, their films land in your real Slate folders and the report lists them for you to delete. The transcript checks, including the no-browser check, run as usual.
The eval's session stays in main's session list (agent:main:slate-eval-…).

The sandbox notice reaches main at the top of its message (notice_in_message). Main reads its instructions from its own workspace (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md and USER.md in ~/oneiro/runtime/workspace, agents.entries.main.workspace in ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json), never from the eval's folder, and `openclaw agent` takes no extra system prompt; changing main's workspace or config is the owner's call.
Main's tools run in that workspace (tools_cwd), so a relative path it writes lands in Oneiro's workspace: stays_in_sandbox reads its writes from there.
not_exercised: First live run, 2026-10-01: the session id comes back under result.meta.agentMeta.sessionId and is found there; `openclaw transcripts path <id> --transcript` answers 'transcripts session not found' for agent turns on 2026.9.4, so the transcript comes from the chat.history fallback, which carries every tool call and its result.

oneiro-strategist.label: Oneiro's strategist, one answer-only Codex call on a pursuit snapshot

how: The engine's cloud steps call runCodex with answerOnly: --sandbox read-only, --ephemeral, --ignore-user-config, and the 13 features in ANSWER_ONLY_DISABLED switched off, so the model answers from its prompt with no shell, browser or tools. The model and effort are llm.js's cloud defaults (gpt-6-astra, high; OCA_CODEX_MODEL=gpt-6-astra in the LaunchAgent).

The prompt is buildTextPrompt's shape: the strategist's system prompt, a blank line, then 'User: ' and the message strategize() composes. The system prompt is read from agents.js at run time; the message is composed from the pursuit's snapshot (slate/evals/strategist.py).
deviations: Recent agent work, actions, durable dispositions and charter grants come from the engine's database; the dry run leaves them at the engine's own empty defaults.
not_exercised: No live run in the build session; the case stays pending until the self-want lands.
